extracted.intended_audience: early-career, tenure-track assistant professors (potential applicants to the NSF CAREER program, CBET/ENG)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for preparing and submitting an NSF CAREER proposal (CBET/ENG), including required components, page/budget limits, integration of research and education, review criteria, eligibility, and submission policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required proposal components (front & back end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Front end includes Cover Sheet; Back end includes Biographical Sketch (2 pages), Project Summary (1 page), Departmental Letter (2 pages), Project Description (15 pages), Budget (five years, $500,000 total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Summary must contain Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts. Biographical Sketch limited to 2 pages and should include Research and Education Accomplishments. Project Description must cover proposed research, proposed education activities, integration with research, and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Sheet title requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cover Sheet must include 'CAREER:' in the Title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical Sketch limited to 2 pages and should document Research and Education Accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary limited to 1 page and must address Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental letter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Departmental Letter limited to 2 pages and should describe activities supported by the institution and the career development of the PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description content and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description limited to 15 pages and must include the Proposed Research Project & Plan; Proposed Education Activities; Integration with Research; and Assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the education activities are integrated with the research and include assessment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget covers five years with a total of $500,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of research and education
rubrics_metrics.description: CAREER proposals must have an integrated research & education plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose creative research and education plans and explain how they will be integrated and assessed. Envision how the research program will impact educational goals and how education activities will feed back to the research. Balance research and education and avoid "over proposing" activities (quality over quantity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit (NSF review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review questions include: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts? Is there a well-reasoned, well-organized plan based on a sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success? Are the PI's qualifications sufficient? Are adequate resources available to the PI/PI team at home and collaborator institutions?

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts (NSF review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider advancement of discovery while promoting teaching, training, and learning; broad dissemination to enhance scientific and technological understanding (e.g., outreach); participation of under-represented groups in STEM; educational impact including undergraduate and K-12 activities; and other ways the project will benefit society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should demonstrate both strong intellectual merit (research & education) and clear broader impacts (broadening participation and societal benefit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate advancement/contribution of knowledge, creativity/originality, organization of the proposal, qualifications of PI, adequacy of resources, educational impact, outreach and dissemination, and engagement of under-represented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research vs. Education content balance and page guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Research portion typically 10-12 pages; Education portion typically 3-5 pages within the Project Description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a vision for a five-year research & education program that leads to a lifetime of contributions. Research should be creative, advance knowledge, and be well-conceived; education and outreach should be inspired by the research, well conceived and integrated with research, include assessment/evaluation, and engage under-represented groups in STEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal concept feedback process
rubrics_metrics.description: Before full submission, applicants should submit a Proposal Concept / one-page summary (addressing Intellectual Merit & Broader Impacts) to the Program Director for feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the desired Program Description on the NSF website, email a one-page summary to the PD, request PD feedback by email, schedule phone calls or visits (provide list of questions 24 hours before the call), and consider visiting NSF Arlington, VA for discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: faculty rank and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only assistant professors without tenure are eligible; associate professors (with or without tenure) are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is determined by the effective date of your appointment at your university. You must remain in a tenure-track Assistant Professor (or equivalent) position until the October 1st following your proposal submission deadline to be eligible. Do not submit if you anticipate your title will change to Associate Professor on or before that October 1st.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes for return without review
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain submission errors will cause a proposal to be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: listing a co-principal investigator (co-PI) on a CAREER proposal; PI did not submit to the current CAREER solicitation; departmental letter is missing. (If any of these occur the proposal will be returned.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent NSF funding and proposal duplication rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Having another NSF grant does not preclude CAREER eligibility, but duplicate or substantially similar proposals submitted concurrently are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of the CAREER proposal must be significantly different from other active NSF proposals so it does not appear to be a resubmission of the same proposal. Submitting duplicate or substantially similar proposals concurrently to more than one program without prior NSF approval will result in return of the redundant proposal. Do not submit the same work both as a CAREER and as a regular research proposal concurrently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: CAREER proposals are reviewed primarily by panel review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels (rather than mainly ad-hoc/mail review) are the primary review method for CAREER proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: One CAREER proposal per competition rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may submit only one CAREER proposal per competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not submit two CAREER proposals to two different Programs, Divisions, or Directorates in the same competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan for education component
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation plan is required to assess the education component; an outside evaluator is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should have some sort of evaluation plan to provide feedback for future improvements. If you have not done evaluations before, seek someone within your organization (e.g., education department or existing course evaluation systems) to help adapt evaluation methods. Use internal collaborators if external evaluators are not available.
